name: Udaipur
description: Udaipur is a lakeside city in southern Rajasthan, built around a series of interconnected lakes and dominated by grand Rajput-era palaces. It suits travelers drawn to heritage architecture, romantic ambience, and bazaar culture, but rewards those willing to walk its hilly old city lanes rather than sticking to tourist circuits. Crowds and commercialization are heavy near the lake ghats, so honest planning helps manage expectations.
bases: Old City (Lal Ghat / Gangaur Ghat area)
nearest_airport: Maharana Pratap Airport, Dabok (UDR) — approx. 22 km from city centre

attractions.name: City Palace
attractions.description: The largest palace complex in Rajasthan, built over roughly 400 years by successive Mewar rulers. The museum inside is genuinely rich in miniature paintings, armoury, and courtyards, though crowds peak between 10 am and 2 pm.
attractions.base: Old City (Lal Ghat / Gangaur Ghat area)

attractions.name: Lake Pichola Boat Ride
attractions.description: A man-made lake dating to 1362, best experienced on the government-run boat that stops at Jag Mandir island. Views of the City Palace from the water are iconic but the ride itself is short and can feel rushed.
attractions.base: Old City (Lal Ghat / Gangaur Ghat area)

attractions.name: Jag Mandir Island Palace
attractions.description: A palace complex built on an island in Lake Pichola, accessible by boat from the City Palace jetty. The gardens and lakeside seating are pleasant; entry is separate from the boat fee and the interior halls are modest.
attractions.base: Old City (Lal Ghat / Gangaur Ghat area)

attractions.name: Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace)
attractions.description: A hilltop palace built in 1884 overlooking Udaipur and the Aravalli range, offering the best panoramic sunset views in the area. The building interior is largely empty; the drive up through wildlife sanctuary forest and the view from the ramparts are the real draw.

attractions.name: Fateh Sagar Lake
attractions.description: A reservoir north of the old city with a lakeside promenade popular with locals in the evenings. It lacks the heritage drama of Pichola but feels more authentic; the embankment is good for a stroll and light street food.

attractions.name: Saheliyon Ki Bari
attractions.description: An 18th-century royal garden with fountains, kiosks, and a small museum, originally built for the queen's handmaidens. It is compact, well-maintained, and genuinely pleasant on a cool morning, though it takes under an hour.

attractions.name: Jagdish Temple
attractions.description: A large 17th-century Indo-Aryan temple dedicated to Vishnu, located a short walk from the City Palace main gate. It is an active place of worship with fine carved stone work; go early to avoid tour groups and to see morning aarti.
attractions.base: Old City (Lal Ghat / Gangaur Ghat area)

attractions.name: Bagore Ki Haveli
attractions.description: An 18th-century lakeside haveli on Gangaur Ghat with 138 rooms displaying costumes, manuscripts, and royal artefacts. The evening folk dance performance (Dharohar Show) is the most authentic cultural program in the city.
attractions.base: Old City (Lal Ghat / Gangaur Ghat area)

attractions.name: Shilpgram
attractions.description: A rural arts and crafts complex set on the edge of Fateh Sagar lake, showcasing traditional dwellings and crafts from five west-Indian states. It is rarely crowded, genuinely educational for children, and the annual December fair is outstanding; outside festival season the exhibits feel sparse.

attractions.name: Badi Lake (Jaisamand Road)
attractions.description: A large, rarely-visited reservoir about 12 km from the city centre, flanked by the Aravalli hills and frequented by migratory birds and local fishermen. Almost no foreign tourists come here; it is a genuine local escape with good birdwatching in winter and a completely unhurried atmosphere.
